claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an FCC matrix.
Trace yttrium addition strengthens adhesion of the alloy's protective oxide scale.
Improved oxide-scale adhesion reduces degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing gases.
Improved oxide-scale adhesion delays catastrophic failure.
Yttrium segregates to the oxide/alloy interface during high-temperature exposure.
Interfacial yttrium modifies oxide composition and microstructure.
Yttrium-induced changes in oxide composition and microstructure enhance oxide-scale adhesion.
A more adherent oxide scale provides better protection against further oxidation.
A more adherent oxide scale limits stress accumulation that could otherwise cause scale spallation or catastrophic failure.
Relative to undoped material, yttrium-doped specimens will form a more uniform and adherent oxide layer under matched high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
Relative to undoped material, yttrium-doped specimens will exhibit lower degradation rates and delayed or mitigated catastrophic failure.
The undoped alloy develops less-adherent oxide scales that cause faster degradation and a higher probability of failure.
The proposed behavior applies primarily at high temperature in oxidizing environments.
Prior literature on similar alloys supports a beneficial role of yttrium in oxide-scale adhesion.

contradictions.description: The baseline extends the less-adherent-scale and faster-degradation behavior to oxidizing or reducing conditions, whereas the boundary and uncertainty fields state that validity under strongly reducing conditions is uncertain and not established.
